title: Sunday Pot Roast with Potatoes & Carrots
description: A classic slow-cooked Sunday roast with tender potatoes, carrots, and rich savory gravy.
equipment: large skillet if using slow cooker

steps.text: Brown the roast for deeper flavor.
Add broth and seasonings and cook slowly until tender.
Add potatoes and carrots and finish until everything is fork-tender.

cookSteps.text: Pat {{roast}} chuck roast dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat {{oil}} oil and brown roast well on both sides, about 4–5 minutes per side.
Add {{broth}} beef broth, {{worcestershire}} Worcestershire sauce, and {{thyme}} thyme. Cover and cook at 325°F for about 2 1/2 hours (or use a slow cooker on LOW).
Add {{potatoes}} baby potatoes and {{carrots}} carrots. Cover and continue cooking until vegetables are tender and beef pulls apart easily, about 1 1/2 hours.
Rest beef 10 minutes before serving with vegetables and pan juices.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze portions up to 3 months.

title: Sunday Herb Roast Chicken
description: A golden whole chicken roasted with herbs, potatoes, and carrots for a traditional Sunday supper.

steps.text: Season the chicken and arrange vegetables around it.
Roast until deeply golden and safely cooked.
Rest before carving so the juices settle.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 425°F. Pat {{chicken}} whole chicken dry. Rub with {{fat}} butter or olive oil, {{thyme}} thyme, {{garlic}} garlic powder, salt, and pepper. Arrange {{potatoes}} potatoes and {{carrots}} carrots around it.
Roast 20 minutes, then reduce oven to 375°F and continue roasting until the thickest part of the thigh reaches 165°F, about 60–70 minutes more.
Rest chicken 15 minutes before carving.

storage: Refrigerate chicken and vegetables up to 4 days.

title: Sunday Meatloaf, Mashed Potatoes & Gravy
description: Old-fashioned meatloaf served with creamy mashed potatoes and simple savory gravy.

steps.text: Boil and mash the potatoes while it cooks.
Make a quick pan-style gravy and serve together.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 375°F. Gently mix {{meat}} meat, {{crumbs}} breadcrumbs, {{egg}} egg, 1/2 cup milk, salt, pepper, and preferred seasonings. Shape into a loaf.
Bake until the center reaches 160°F for beef or 165°F for turkey, about 55–65 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil {{potatoes}} peeled potato chunks until fork-tender, about 15–20 minutes. Drain and mash with {{butter}} butter and the remaining 1/4 cup milk.
For gravy, melt 1 tablespoon butter, whisk in {{flour}} flour for 1 minute, then slowly whisk in {{broth}} broth. Simmer until thickened, about 5 minutes.
Rest meatloaf 10 minutes before slicing. Serve with mashed potatoes and gravy.

title: Sunday Glazed Ham with Scalloped Potatoes
description: Sweet-savory glazed ham paired with creamy layered scalloped potatoes for a classic family dinner.

steps.text: Layer sliced potatoes with a simple cream sauce.
Bake potatoes until tender and browned.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 350°F. Place {{ham}} fully cooked ham cut-side down in roasting pan, cover, and bake about 60 minutes.
Melt {{butter}} butter, whisk in {{flour}} flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in {{milk}} milk. Simmer until lightly thickened. Season with salt and pepper.
Layer {{potatoes}} potatoes and sauce in a greased baking dish. Cover and bake 60 minutes.
Mix {{sugar}} brown sugar and {{honey}} honey. Brush over ham and bake uncovered 15–20 minutes. Uncover potatoes for their final 20–30 minutes until tender and browned.
Rest ham 10 minutes before slicing.

title: Salisbury Steak with Mushroom Gravy
description: Tender seasoned beef patties simmered in mushroom gravy—made for mashed potatoes and a quiet Sunday supper.

steps.text: Shape and brown the seasoned patties.
Cook mushrooms and make gravy in the same skillet.
Return patties and simmer until tender and cooked through.

cookSteps.text: Mix {{meat}} ground beef or turkey, {{crumbs}} breadcrumbs, {{egg}} egg, salt, and pepper. Shape into 4 oval patties.
Brown patties over medium heat about 4 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate.
Cook {{mushrooms}} sliced mushrooms in the skillet until softened, about 5 minutes. Sprinkle with {{flour}} flour and stir 1 minute.
Slowly stir in {{broth}} broth and {{worcestershire}} Worcestershire sauce. Return patties, cover, and simmer 15–20 minutes until cooked through and gravy is thick.

storage: Refrigerate patties with gravy up to 4 days.

title: Sunday Three-Cheese Lasagna
description: Layers of pasta, marinara, ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan baked into a bubbling Sunday-dinner centerpiece.

steps.text: Boil noodles and mix the cheese filling.
Build alternating layers of sauce, noodles, and cheese.
Bake until bubbling, then rest before cutting.

cookSteps.text: Heat oven to 375°F. Boil {{noodles}} lasagna noodles until just al dente and drain.
Mix {{ricotta}} ricotta, {{egg}} egg, half of the {{parmesan}} Parmesan, and 1 cup of the mozzarella.
Spread {{sauce}} marinara in a 9x13 dish, then layer noodles, ricotta mixture, {{mozzarella}} mozzarella, and sauce. Repeat, finishing with sauce and remaining cheeses.
Cover and bake 35 minutes. Uncover and bake 15 minutes more until bubbling and browned.
Rest lasagna 15 minutes before slicing.

storage: Refrigerate up to 4 days or freeze individual portions up to 3 months.
